season.lesson: Started Josh Downs (5.7) over Stefon Diggs sitting on the bench (15.5) in the flex — 9.8 points left on the table. Separately, Zay Flowers' 26-point day ended in a hamstring re-injury that's now clouding Week 2; watch practice reports closely on players who leave games early even when the box score looks great.

Tyler Shough (22.38, waiver QB stash) outscored started QB Justin Herbert (9.88) by 12.5 — not a real swap given Shough's a Saints starter you don't play, but the bigger miss was starting Michael Wilson (3.8) over bench WR Josh Downs (14.2), a 10.4-point gap; the Week 3 lineup already has that fixed. Also: Zay Flowers stayed rostered through a scoreless Week 2 (ruled Out, no IR move) — a wasted bench spot two weeks running.

Michael Wilson (25.9) outscored started Josh Downs (12.7) by 13.2 on the bench — the second straight week a bench WR beat a starter by double digits. Backup QB Tyler Shough (24.8) also beat Herbert (13.74) again. Tempting as that pattern looks, don't chase last week's points by benching your clearly better asset — see this week's Do Now, where that exact overcorrection is sitting live in your Week 4 lineup.

news.headline: Saints RB Travis Etienne Jr. to sit with hamstring injury
news.summary: Etienne has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Falcons after the same hamstring that limited him in Week 3 practice flared up again, with no firm return timeline and an IR move still possible.

news.headline: Wide Receiver Michael Wilson Signs Three-Year Contract Extension
news.summary: Wilson signed a three-year, $75M extension with $47M guaranteed, cementing his status as Arizona's real WR1 ahead of Marvin Harrison Jr. in the target hierarchy.

news.headline: Chig Okonkwo Misses Practice on Wednesday
news.summary: Okonkwo remains sidelined by the hamstring injury that has now cost him practice time three straight weeks, with no clear timetable to return.

news.headline: 49ers DE Nick Bosa expected to miss multiple weeks with calf injury
news.summary: Bosa is expected to miss multiple weeks with a calf injury, and the team is still deciding whether to place him on IR, which would keep him out at least through Week 6.

SLEEPER — FAAB: $88 of $100 remaining (unchanged since last week — waiver_budget_used still $12, so last week's Coleman/Freiermuth/Malik Washington bids never went in). Fresh board for this week's Tuesday processing:
1. Ollie Gordon (RB, MIA) — the clear #1 add across all of Sleeper right now (7.8M adds, by far the hottest name on the wire). De'Von Achane is dealing with a shoulder issue and Jaylen Wright just got ruled Out, leaving Gordon (himself Questionable, ribs) as Miami's lead back on paper. Speculative but real bellcow-emergency upside. Drop Woody Marks (buried behind Montgomery in Houston's committee). FAAB $16.
2. Kenyon Sadiq (TE, NYJ) — directly fixes your TE depth: the rookie is already earning real trust in Geno Smith's offense and doubles as insurance for the Week 7 Strange bye. Drop Devaughn Vele (healthy again but a buried WR4 in New Orleans with no real role). FAAB $8.
3. Keaton Mitchell (RB, LAC) — McDaniel says he'll use Hampton, Mitchell, and Vidal 'probably every game.' Adding your own RB1's committee-mate gives you a direct line into that backfield instead of a blind handcuff elsewhere. Drop Tank Bigsby (stuck behind Barkley in Philly, no standalone path). FAAB $6.
Total if you take all three: $30, leaving ~$58 banked for the Week 7 bye scramble (JAX hits Strange, Tuten, AND your DEF all at once) and any Week 12 trade-deadline pushes.
Skipping a forced 4th/5th claim — nothing else on the wire this week is worth a roster spot over what you're already holding.
Hold, don't drop: Stefon Diggs — still WAS's real WR2 by depth chart, more valuable than any add on this week's board. Tyler Shough — goes back to the bench once you revert this week's lineup (see Do Now), but keep him as your Week 7 QB streamer since New Orleans' bye is Week 8, not 7.
